region: Bonner and Boundary counties — Sandpoint, Sagle, Ponderay, Dover, Priest River, Clark Fork, Hope, Coolin, Bonners Ferry.
disclaimer: Not legal advice, not a perc test, not a listing service. Public records and local trades. Confirm with PHD, IDWR, the county, and a licensed outfit before you write a check.

uses.label: A house already on it
uses.hint: You are buying a home plus acres, not starting from dirt.

uses.label: Kitchen garden
uses.hint: Beds, berries, a few fruit trees. Short season.

uses.label: Orchard
uses.hint: Apples, cherries, cold-hardy stock. Frost pockets matter.

uses.label: Greenhouse or high tunnel
uses.hint: Extends the season. Snow load is real.

uses.label: Chickens and small stock
uses.hint: Coop, predators, well setbacks from the run.

uses.label: Cattle or ranching
uses.hint: Hay ground, water, fence. Not a timber lot with a dream.

uses.label: Horses
uses.hint: Dry turnout, arena or round pen, winter hay.

uses.label: Hay ground
uses.hint: Open, not timber. Irrigation or decent rain-fed meadow.

uses.label: Timber
uses.hint: Manage, heat, or a selective cut. Fire and access.

uses.label: Shop, barn, or equipment
uses.hint: Power, approach, snow, and a building permit.

uses.label: Lake or river
uses.hint: IDL shoreline rules. Flood and setbacks.

uses.label: Hunt and timber recreation
uses.hint: Privacy, game, often steep and snowy.

uses.label: Off-grid or thin power
uses.hint: Legal here with the right system. Not cheaper up front.

uses.label: Guest cabin or second dwelling
uses.hint: Zoning and extra septic. AF and R lots differ.

musts.label: Power at the road or house

places.name: Sagle timber acres
places.blurb: The classic relocator lot: trees, a driveway rumor, and a listing that says buildable. You will spend on well, septic, and a real road before a garden looks like a magazine.
places.water: Often no log on file, or a neighbor log. Plan $20–40k+ to drill. Storage if the well is shy.
places.septic: Vacant timber is a PHD site eval during inspection, not a vibe. Mound money if the draw is wet.
places.access: Private easements. Ask who plows. A gentleman’s agreement is not legal access.
places.zoning: Often rural / AF. Extra dwelling is not automatic.
places.winter: Shade holds snow. South openings matter for garden and solar.

notes.water: Pull neighbor well logs in the same section before you offer.
notes.septic: Timber duff is not soil. PHD wants a hole and a perc, not pine needles.
notes.access: Get the recorded easement. Highway district will not maintain a private spur.
notes.fire: Defensible space is insurance, not aesthetics. BonFire fuels work is nearby.

places.name: Selle valley meadow
places.area: Selle / north and east of Sandpoint
places.blurb: Open ground that can actually grow hay. You are buying water, fence, and whether the well and septic match the house — not the barn in the photos.
places.water: Well on file more often. Ask GPM and a recent pump test. Irrigation is a water-right question, not a hose.
places.septic: Existing system. Confirm it was finaled and sized for the bedrooms you think you bought.
places.access: More county road than Sagle timber, still confirm plow route.
places.zoning: AF lots show up here. Ag exemption is paperwork with the assessor, not a lifestyle.
places.winter: Wind on open ground. Hay storage and a shop you can get a tractor into.

notes.water: Domestic well ≠ irrigation right. IDWR if you want to flood a meadow.
notes.livestock: Fence-out state. Wolves and cougars are not a meme. Hay budget before cute stock.
notes.zoning: Second dwelling and farm labor housing have different paths. Read the ordinance.

places.name: Cocolalla / Westmond house-plus-acres
places.area: Cocolalla, Westmond, south toward Athol edge
places.blurb: The starter homestead: a 1970s–2000s house, a well that works until it does not, and a septic that has never been pumped in the listing photos.
places.water: Log should exist. 4–8 GPM with a tank is common. Test for coliform during inspection.
places.septic: Age the tank. Replacement field room. PHD record search before you waive inspection.
places.access: Often on a named road. Still ask about the hill in January.
places.zoning: Smaller lots. Extra dwelling is the fight.
places.winter: Doable. Wood or propane backup when the well pump rides the outage.

notes.septic: A 1994 gravity field can be fine or finished. The record tells you which.
notes.winter: If the pump is in a pit without heat, you will learn that in February.

places.name: Priest River / Pend Oreille bottoms
places.area: Priest River, Dover flats, low Pend Oreille ground
places.blurb: Looks like a deal because it floods, sits wet, or fights a drainfield. Cheap dirt is expensive water.
places.water: High water table. Wells can be shallow and unhappy. Surface water is not a domestic right you just take.
places.septic: Mound and capping-fill country. Budget the high end or walk.
places.access: County roads exist. Spring thaw eats driveways.
places.zoning: Floodplain and wetland overlays eat building envelope.
places.winter: Ice and a high water table. Not a basement plan.

notes.septic: If PHD says mound, believe them. Creek lots fail setbacks quietly.
notes.zoning: Flood maps and wetlands are the deal. A pretty spring is a warning.

places.name: Clark Fork bench and canyon
places.blurb: Quiet, steep, and a longer winter. You are choosing isolation on purpose. Power and a plow plan are the purchase.
places.water: Drill cost can jump with rock. Neighbor logs in the same section.
places.septic: Slope and rock. Site eval is not optional.
places.access: Private spurs. County does not love your hill. School bus is a fantasy some years.
places.winter: This is the test. Wood, generator, and a vehicle that starts.

notes.access: Who plows, with what, under what written agreement.
notes.power: NLI or Avista line extension vs solar+generator. Run the real number.
notes.winter: Clark Fork is not Sandpoint. Plan a week without a store.

places.name: Boundary County farm ground
places.blurb: More working ag than the Sandpoint lifestyle lots. You still confirm well, septic, and whether the hay ground is actually hay.
places.water: Better chance of a serious well. Irrigation is still a right, not a vibe.
places.septic: House system plus any shop bathroom. PHD still owns the permit (or the local health path — confirm).
places.zoning: Ag is the point. Brands, fence, and assessor exemption.
places.winter: Open and cold. Equipment that runs in January.

notes.livestock: Idaho brand. Fence-out. Hay inventory before calving stories.
notes.soil: Ask what actually came off this ground last three years, not what the listing planted in 1998.

places.name: Hope / east Pend Oreille
places.blurb: You are paying for the lake. IDL, setbacks, and a septic that cannot creep toward the water. Livestock is a poor fit.
places.water: Community or individual well. Lake is not your tap.
places.septic: Setbacks to the lake are the whole game. 100–300 ft from surface water.
places.access: Better roads, steep drives to the water.
places.zoning: Shoreline and IDL encroachment for docks.
places.winter: Beautiful and slick. Ice on the drive.

notes.septic: Lake lots fail on setback more than on soil.
notes.zoning: Dock and shoreline are IDL, not a handshake with a neighbor.

places.name: Ponderay / city-edge shop lot
places.blurb: For the tradesperson who needs a shop and a short drive to town, not a ranch. Sewer or septic depends on the street.
places.water: City or community in pockets; well on the fringe.
places.septic: Sewer if you are lucky. If not, small-lot replacement field is the constraint.
places.zoning: City/county mix. Shop use and home occupation rules.
places.winter: The easy one. Still a generator for the well or sump if you are on a well.

notes.zoning: A 40x60 shop is a permit and a neighbor issue. Ask before you close.
notes.power: Three-phase is a unicorn. Confirm the panel before the welder.

steps.title: Your plan
steps.objective: What this place is for: garden, stock, timber, shop, or a house you can winter.
steps.why: Lots that look the same in photos fail different plans. Cattle want meadow. A high tunnel wants sun. A shop wants power and a legal approach.

tasks.text: What you want the land to do — garden, stock, timber, shop, a house you can winter — is how similar-looking lots fail different plans.
The listing price is not the whole bill. Well, septic, and the first winter sit on top of it.
Acreage bands matter here: ten timber acres is not twenty hay acres.

steps.legal: No permit yet. This is the free look. Everything after is an office or a check.

steps.title: Water first
steps.objective: How the parcel drinks: well log, GPM, storage, and whether irrigation is a right.
steps.why: Rural Bonner is wells. The log and a pump test tell you whether a house and stock make it through August.

tasks.text: Pull an IDWR well log for the parcel. A listing that says the area is good is not a log.
Gallons per minute and storage matter. Four GPM can run a house; fifteen is comfort. Stock and irrigation want more.
A water test and a pump test during inspection are cheap compared to a dry August.
Hay or orchard irrigation needs a water right. A garden hose is not one.

records.name: How to pull a well log

steps.legal: Domestic wells are regulated. Irrigation and stockwater can need a right. IDWR is the office. A neighbor’s ditch story is not.

steps.title: What the ground will take
steps.objective: The PHD record, or a site eval before anyone waives inspection.
steps.why: Off city sewer, you are buying a septic system. Creek lots and high water tables can turn a gravity field into a mound.

tasks.text: Start with the parcel number from the assessor.
Panhandle Health keeps septic records by section.
A finaled permit and room for a replacement field are the deal, not a tank lid in the grass.
Drainfields want about 100 feet from wells, and setback from creek or lake.

records.name: How to pull a septic record

steps.legal: Panhandle Health District issues the permit in this region (Sandpoint office 2101 W. Pine). They are not the city. New permit fee in the 2026 guidelines: $1,250.

steps.title: A road you can prove
steps.objective: Recorded legal access and a winter plow story.
steps.why: Recorded access and a winter plow story matter as much as the house. A two-track in the photos is not enough.

tasks.text: Legal access is on the deed or title, not a two-track in the listing photos.
Who plows, with what, belongs in writing.
A new driveway often needs an approach permit from the highway district or ITD.
School buses do not always turn around where a listing implies.

steps.legal: Legal access is recorded. Maintenance of a private road is a separate contract. The county will not adopt your spur because you asked.

steps.title: What you may build
steps.objective: Plain-English zoning: extra dwelling, shop, AF ground or a rural house lot.
steps.why: R and AF lots around Sandpoint are not the same. Extra dwellings, shops, and farm labor housing each have a path — or they do not.

tasks.text: Look up zoning on the county map, not the listing adjective.
Guest cabins and second dwellings depend on the zone.
Shop size, height, and home-occupation rules are Planning questions before anyone pours a slab.
An ag exemption follows use at the assessor, not a barn photo.

steps.legal: Zoning and building permits are county (or city if you are in one). We are not your planner. Bring the parcel number to the counter.

steps.title: Power and heat
steps.objective: Avista, Northern Lights, or a real off-grid number — plus wood and propane for when the line dies.
steps.why: The well pump rides the outage. Heat is wood, propane, electric, or a mix. Off-grid is legal with the right system.

tasks.text: Confirm which utility serves the place: Avista, Northern Lights, Inland Power, or none.
No line means a line-extension estimate in writing before you close.
A generator or battery plan for the well pump and a freezer is local common sense.
Heat is wood, propane, or both — with dry wood or a delivery account.

steps.legal: Electrical work is licensed. Off-grid still meets code if you pull a building permit. Utility easements are on the title work.

steps.title: Growing season
steps.objective: Frost, sun, and whether this dirt grows food or only trees.
steps.why: Sandpoint’s season is short. Frost pockets in draws are hard on orchards. Hay wants open ground.

tasks.text: Garden and hay want winter sun, not a north timber wall.
Late spring and early fall frost are normal here.
If you want hay or cattle, ask what actually came off the field.
Garden water needs well gallons and a frost-free hydrant plan.

steps.legal: Selling produce has cottage-food and scale rules. A kitchen garden for the house does not. Irrigation water is still IDWR.

steps.title: Stock and fence
steps.objective: Fence, hay, predators, and brands — before the trailer shows up.
steps.why: Idaho is a fence-out state. Wolves and cougars work this country. Stock on timber acres is a hay bill.

tasks.text: Winter hay math comes before the animals.
Fence has to hold your stock and respect the neighbor.
Cattle: Idaho brand through ISDA.
Manure and runs sit away from the well and the drainfield.

records.name: Idaho State Dept. of Agriculture — brands

steps.legal: Brands, health papers on interstate stock, and CAFO rules if you get big. We are not your vet or the brand inspector.

steps.title: Fire and timber
steps.objective: Defensible space, burn rules, and whether timber is a resource or a fuse.
steps.why: This region burns. A timber lot without a break is winter wood and a July problem.

tasks.text: Defensible space is ongoing, not a listing photo.
Ask a local agent if the address is insurable.
Burn restrictions and who issues a burn permit change with the season.
A timber cut needs access and a logger who will show up.

steps.legal: Burn bans are real. Logging and slash have rules. Insurance underwriting is not the county’s job and not ours.

steps.title: First winter
steps.objective: Tires, wood, water, and a plan for the week the power dies.
steps.why: Town is often 60–70 inches. The mountain is another climate. January is the test, not the showing.

tasks.text: Real winter tires.
Dry wood, or a propane account that will deliver.
Heat on the well pump, or a way to keep water when the line is down.
A week of food and a way to cook it if the power dies.

steps.legal: No office for this one. This is why the rest of the path exists.

steps.title: Listings & types
steps.objective: Live listings, then how Bonner and Boundary country actually behaves.
steps.why: Sagle timber, Selle hay, Priest River bottoms, Clark Fork benches, and Boundary farms are different purchases.

tasks.text: Live listings are the market. Types on this site are how the country behaves.
A property type is optional. Skip it if you are still learning the country.
Drive that country in daylight and after a rain before you offer.

steps.legal: We do not list MLS. Types are how the region actually works. An agent or FSBO does the contract.

steps.title: Who can help
steps.objective: Licensed local outfits for the work this place needs.
steps.why: Septic, well, excavator, electrician — pointed at the country you picked, or the whole region.

tasks.text: Bonner County Planning is the office before a slab.
Call a licensed local outfit yourself. The directory is a starting list.

steps.legal: Licensed trades for electrical, plumbing, septic, well. Owner-builder has limits. We intro you to names; we do not take a cut of the job.

steps.title: Your notes
steps.objective: A recap of the plan you saved. It stays on this computer.
steps.why: This page is a recap of what you marked for listings. We do not get a copy.
steps.legal: Not legal advice, not a perc test, not a listing service. Confirm with PHD, IDWR, the county, and a licensed outfit before you write a check.
